context:
Tests whether an agent asked only to write a markdown decision artefact nevertheless applies the git-workflow skill before its first edit: branches per artefact, isolates into a worktree because the checkout is dirty, derives the fork point rather than reading it from configuration, and — because the artefact is an ADR, a decision, and the repository has no remote to propose it on — stops with the branch and its worktree kept for a human to merge. Under ADR 0003 a branch that adds an ADR is merged by a human, never by the agent; with no remote there is nowhere to propose it, so nothing is merged and nothing is cleaned up.

IMPORTANT — task.md deliberately says nothing about git. It asks for an ADR and nothing else. Every git property scored below must therefore come from the skill being loaded, not from the agent following instructions. An agent that writes a good ADR straight into the working tree and stops has written the deliverable and failed this scenario, which is the intended discrimination.

The fixture is built by setup.sh before the agent runs. Inspect the result with shell and git, in the solution directory (`solution/`, which is a git repository; paths below are relative to it). The fixture leaves:
- branches `main` and `dev`, divergent from a shared base. `dev` carries `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` and not `RELEASE-NOTES.md`; `main` carries `RELEASE-NOTES.md` and not the discovery note. Forking from one therefore produces a visibly different tree from forking from the other.
- two anchor tags marking where the fixture ended: `fixture-base-dev` (the tip of `dev`) and `fixture-base-main` (the tip of `main`). Use them; every criterion below is phrased against them so that nothing has to be guessed.
- HEAD on `dev` with a dirty working tree: a modified `README.md`, an untracked `benchmark-notes.txt`, and an untracked `.venv/`.
- gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`, and gitignored `node_modules/`, both with real contents.
- no remote at all.
- two decoys naming the wrong trunk: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which states that branches are cut from `main`, that `dev` must not be branched from, that the trunk is recorded in git configuration, that branches are named `feature/<initials>-<description>`, and that changes are squash-merged through a GitHub pull request; and the local git configuration keys `workflow.trunk=main` and `init.defaultBranch=main`.

The artefact the task asks for is a new ADR under `docs/adr/`, which in this fixture's numbering is `0003`. Call its file `<ADR>`. Call the artefact branch `<branch>`: the single ref named by `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/heads/adr-*'` (use for-each-ref rather than `git branch --list`, which prefixes a branch checked out in a worktree with `+`). Call its worktree `<wt>`: the second entry of `git worktree list`, expected at `.worktrees/<branch>`.

Score from git state and the working tree only. Do not score from any transcript, log or summary the agent may have written; if a property is not visible in the repository, it is not evidence here.

checklist.name: Trunk untouched: the decision was not merged by the agent
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless `<branch>` exists and `git ls-tree -r --name-only <branch> -- docs/adr/` includes a third ADR file; an agent that never produced the artefact has not demonstrated restraint, it has done nothing. Given that: `git rev-parse dev` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-dev` and `git rev-parse main` equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-main`; `git log --oneline fixture-base-dev..dev` and `git log --oneline fixture-base-main..main` both print nothing. FAILS IF: `dev` acquired a merge of the ADR branch, which is the agent merging a decision itself — the behaviour ADR 0003 reserves for a human; or acquired the ADR as a direct, squashed or fast-forwarded commit; or `main` moved at all.

checklist.name: Artefact branch kept, carrying the committed ADR, in the numbered form
checklist.description: `<branch>` is the only `adr-*` branch and is named `adr-0003-<slug>`, where the slug matches the new ADR file's slug. `git log --format=%H fixture-base-dev..<branch>` lists at least one commit and the ADR file is in `<branch>`'s tree, committed. FAILS IF: no such branch exists, because the ADR was written straight into a working tree or because the branch was deleted as if it had merged; or the ADR is uncommitted; or the branch is named in CONTRIBUTING.md's `feature/<initials>-...` form, or without the number, or with a number that disagrees with the file's.

checklist.name: Isolated into a worktree that is still present, primary checkout on dev
checklist.description: The fixture leaves the primary checkout on `dev` with a dirty tree, so the contention check must select isolation. All of: (a) `.git/logs/HEAD` contains NO line matching `checkout: moving from dev to ` — the fixture leaves none, so any such line means the work was branched in place; (b) `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in the primary checkout is `dev`; (c) `git worktree list` shows `<wt>` at a path ending `/.worktrees/<branch>`, checked out on `<branch>`, and the directory exists and is populated. `git worktree list` may mark it `prunable` because the scoring copy sits at a different absolute path from where the agent ran; that marker is an artefact of the relocation, not of the agent, and is not a failure when the directory is populated. FAILS IF: (a) fails; or the worktree was removed — cleanup after a merge that did not happen, which destroys the human's ability to pick the work up; or the primary checkout is on `<branch>` or on `main`.

checklist.name: The primary checkout's own files are untouched
checklist.description: `solution/README.md` still ends with the line `TODO(orchard): document the retry budget before the 1.5 release.` and that modification is still uncommitted. `solution/benchmark-notes.txt` still exists, still uncommitted, and still contains both fixture lines beginning `2026-09-18: p99 1.8s at 400 rps`. Neither appears in any commit: `git log --all --oneline -- benchmark-notes.txt` is empty, and no commit reachable from any ref touches those README lines. `git stash list` is empty. Do NOT score whether the two files are staged or unstaged: the eval harness stages files in the solution directory when it injects its own context, so `M ` / `A ` in `git status --porcelain` is not evidence of agent action and ` M` / `??` cannot be required. FAILS IF: either file's change appears in a commit, which is what a body running `git add -A && git commit` in the primary checkout produces; or a stash remains; or either file was reverted, deleted or lost its fixture content.

checklist.name: Fork point derived as the local dev branch, decoys ignored
checklist.description: The first commit on `<branch>` (`git rev-list --reverse fixture-base-dev..<branch> | head -1`) has `fixture-base-dev` as its parent; `<branch>`'s tree does NOT contain `RELEASE-NOTES.md`; `git merge-base <branch> fixture-base-main` does not equal `fixture-base-main`; and `dev`'s tree still contains `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md`. Do NOT require the discovery note in `<branch>`'s tree: under ADR 0004 a consumed discovery note leaves the tree, so an ADR branch that removes it is correct. The fixture supplies two independent decoys that both say `main` — CONTRIBUTING.md's prose and the `workflow.trunk` / `init.defaultBranch` configuration keys — and ADR 0003 requires the fork point to be derived, never read from per-repository configuration. FAILS IF: the branch forked from `main`; or its tree contains `RELEASE-NOTES.md`.

checklist.name: Configuration copied into the worktree, built dependencies neither carried nor committed
checklist.description: All of: `<wt>/.claude/settings.local.json` exists and contains the fixture's permissions JSON with four `allow` entries, and there is no `<wt>/.claude/.claude`; `<wt>/.venv` and `<wt>/node_modules` do not exist; `solution/.venv/` still exists with its fixture contents; and `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format= | grep -E '^(\.venv|node_modules)/'` finds nothing. `.gitignore` spells the Python directory `venv/`, so `.venv/` is NOT ignored: a body that carried it into the worktree and staged everything commits it. Do NOT score whether gitignored files (`solution/.claude/settings.local.json`, `solution/node_modules/`) remain in the primary checkout: the scoring copy does not preserve gitignored files there. FAILS IF: the settings were not copied into the worktree, or were copied to a nested path; or `.venv/` or `node_modules/` was carried into the worktree or committed; or `.venv/` was deleted from the base checkout.

checklist.name: Bookkeeping rides on the artefact branch
checklist.description: The `.worktrees/` entry is bookkeeping under ADR 0003's classification table, so it rides on the ADR branch: `git show <branch>:.gitignore` contains a `.worktrees/` line; `git log --format=%H fixture-base-dev..<branch> -- .gitignore` names the commit that added it; `git show dev:.gitignore` is unchanged from `git show fixture-base-dev:.gitignore`; and `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` does not list `.gitignore`. Whether it shares a commit with the ADR is not scored; commit cadence is delegated. FAILS IF: the line was committed onto `dev` or took a branch of its own; or it was left uncommitted in the worktree; or it was added in the primary checkout.

checklist.name: Derives-From trailer on the branch's first commit names the upstream artefact exactly
checklist.description: The FIRST commit on `<branch>` after `fixture-base-dev` carries the git trailer `Derives-From: docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` in its trailer block. Check with `git log --reverse --format='%H%n%(trailers:key=Derives-From,valueonly)' fixture-base-dev..<branch>` and read the first entry. FAILS IF: no commit carries it; or it names something else; or the path is not repository-relative; or it appears only as a sentence in the body; or it sits only on a later commit — which is what a body that commits the bookkeeping separately and first produces.

checklist.name: No remote invented to propose the decision
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless `<branch>` exists with the ADR committed. Given that: `git remote -v` prints nothing and `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` lists nothing. With no remote, a decision cannot be proposed and the correct behaviour is to stop and leave it for a human; CONTRIBUTING.md's instruction to open a GitHub pull request does not license inventing a remote. FAILS IF: a remote was added; or refs under `refs/remotes/` exist.
